articles.title: El Betis arranca dispuesto a romper su techo de cristal
articles.standfirst: Es el gran favorito que asigna VERSUS para completar el TOP-4 de LaLiga
articles.summary: Es el gran favorito que asigna VERSUS para completar el TOP-4 de LaLiga
articles.body: El Betis está de vuelta a la Champions más de 20 años después. Lo logró quedando quinto y beneficiándose del cupo extra que logró LaLiga por su desempeño en competiciones europeas la pasada campaña. El proyecto de Manuel Pellegrini, sin embargo, quiere dar un paso más y volver a meterse entre los cuatro primeros de LaLiga. Un objetivo que se presenta como uno de los grandes retos del conjunto verdiblanco esta temporada. Para VERSUS es el gran favorito para acompañar a Barcelona, Real Madrid y Atlético de Madrid en lo más alto de la clasificación. Le asigna una cuota de 2.35 para quedar entre los cuatro primeros, bastante por delante de Athletic Club (3.75), Villarreal (4.0) o Real Sociedad (7). El buen arranque del conjunto verdiblanco también empieza a tener su reflejo en las apuestas deportivas, donde aparece como uno de los principales candidatos para hacerse con esa cuarta plaza. El inicio de temporada está siendo prometedor. El Betis ha vencido por la mínima a Real Sociedad y Valencia, logrando así un pleno de puntos (6/6) en las dos primeras jornadas. Es la tercera vez que el conjunto verdiblanco consigue arrancar con dos triunfos a lo largo de la Era Manuel Pellegrini. Una dinámica que, a la espera de perfilar la plantilla en estos últimos días de mercado, alimenta la ilusión de un equipo que quiere dar un paso adelante en la clasificación. El reto ahora es igualar el arranque de la temporada 2022-23, cuando el Betis fue capaz de sumar los nueve primeros puntos en juego. Es la única vez que el conjunto verdiblanco ha conseguido enlazar tres victorias en las tres primeras jornadas de Primera división a lo largo de toda su historia. Las mejores casas de apuestas ya reflejan el potencial del equipo de Pellegrini... aunque el próximo obstáculo no será sencillo. Su rival para conseguirlo será el Levante, que viene de empatar contra Osasuna a domicilio. El Betis sólo ha ganado en uno de sus cinco últimos desplazamientos al Ciutat de Valencia. Un dato que invita a la prudencia pese al notable inicio de los verdiblancos. VERSUS, aun así, les considera favoritos y asigna una cuota de 2.14 a la victoria del Betis. El objetivo está claro: mantener el pleno y empezar a romper su techo de cristal.

articles.body: La Corte Constitucional de Colombia tomó una decisión determinante respecto a la Ley 2381 sobre la Reforma Pensional, marcando un hito en la arquitectura de la seguridad social del país. El alto tribunal salvó el grueso del nuevo sistema de protección social para la vejez, declarando la exequibilidad de 92 de sus artículos. Sin embargo, ordenó devolver nueve artículos a la Cámara de Representantes para que sean subsanados por vicios de trámite, fijando como nueva fecha de entrada en vigencia del sistema el 1 de abril de 2027. El fallo preservó la estructura de pilares impulsada durante el gobierno de Gustavo Petro, la cual transforma el modelo de competencia entre Colpensiones y los fondos privados hacia un esquema complementario. La Corte Constitucional identificó irregularidades en el debate parlamentario de un grupo específico de artículos, devolviéndolos a la Cámara de Representantes, la cual dispondrá de 30 días hábiles a partir de la notificación formal para tramitarlos y corregir los vicios detectados. articles.title: North Texas Names Ex-Indiana QB Tayven Jackson Week 1 Starter Against Hoosiers
articles.summary: The North Texas Mean Green named former Indiana quarterback Tayven Jackson their Week 1 starter against the Hoosiers.
articles.body: A familiar face will be under center against the defending champions to open the season. The North Texas Mean Green announced on Wednesday morning that fifth-year senior Tayven Jackson will be their starting quarterback for the team's Week 1 road opener against the Indiana Hoosiers on Sept. 5. Jackson beat out sophomores Chaston Ditta and Chris Jimerson Jr. and freshman Ziondre Williams for the starting job. Jackson, who played for the Hoosiers from 2023-24, transferred to North Texas after one season with the UCF Knights. In said season (2025), Jackson totaled 2,151 passing yards, 10 passing touchdowns, eight interceptions and a 126.2 passer rating for the Knights, while completing 63.5% of his passes; he also rushed for three scores. North Texas is the fourth stop in Jackson's collegiate career, as he spent 2022 with the Tennessee Volunteers before transferring to Indiana, with whom he made six starts from 2023-24. Jackson is the younger brother of former Indiana Hoosiers star forward and four-time All-Big Ten honoree Trayce Jackson-Davis, who now plays for the NBA's Toronto Raptors. North Texas is coming off a program-best 12-2 season, but it lost head coach Eric Morris, who left after one season to become the new head coach of the Oklahoma State Cowboys. Former West Virginia Mountaineers and Troy Trojans coach and former Texas Longhorns assistant Neal Brown is the new head coach of the Mean Green. As for Indiana, which is coming off winning its first ever National Championship and is a combined 27-2 under head coach Curt Cignetti, it has former TCU Horned Frogs quarterback Josh Hoover under center, marking the third consecutive season that the Hoosiers find their Week 1 quarterback in the transfer portal (Kurtis Rourke, Fernando Mendoza and Hoover). Over the last two years (2024-25), Hoover has averaged 3,710.5 passing yards, 28 passing touchdowns, 12 interceptions and a 152.2 passer rating per season, while completing 66.2% of his passes. FOX's "Big Noon Kickoff" will be on site in Bloomington for the Week 1 matchup between Indiana and North Texas.

articles.title: Mark Allen: Northern Ireland player extends absence as he misses two more events
articles.summary: Mark Allen will sit out the British Open and English Open for personal reasons, extending his absence from the professional circuit.
articles.body:
Mark Allen will miss the forthcoming British Open and English Open tournaments for personal reasons, the World Snooker Tour has confirmed.

The Northern Ireland player also sat out the recent Championship League, China Open and Wuhan Open ranking events, plus the Shanghai Masters, which is a non-ranking tournament.

His absence from the British and English Opens will mean he has missed the first five ranking events of the season.

The world number 13 is the reigning English Open champion so will not be defending the title he won at Brentwood last year.

Allen's last competitive professional appearance was at the World Championship in Sheffield at the start of May, when he lost a dramatic semi-final against eventual champion Wu Yize 17-16.

The Antrim man agonisingly missed a straight black off its spot in the penultimate frame to win the match before tasting defeat at the hands of the Chinese player.

Allen had been scheduled to face Wang Xinbo in the first round of the British Open and Sam Craigie in his opening match in the English Open.

The British Open takes place from 31 August to 6 September in Cheltenham, with the English Open following from 7 to 13 September.

articles.body: Tiger Woods made a rare public appearance Tuesday through a pre-recorded video message for his longtime friend Notah Begay III, who received the 2026 Payne Stewart Award. The 50-year-old golfer has largely stayed out of public view since his March DUI arrest in Florida. His return on video quickly drew attention, with some fans saying he looked different. Woods is due in court on Sept. 8 over the charges linked to the crash.Tiger Woods sends message to Notah Begay III at Payne Stewart AwardWoods appeared in a video played during the Payne Stewart Award ceremony in Atlanta, where Begay was honored for his work with Native American communities and young people. The PGA Tour said Begay, a four-time PGA Tour winner, was chosen for his character, sportsmanship and charitable work. His NB3 Foundation has reached more than 80,000 Native youth and their families.Woods used the video to look back at a friendship that began when they were young golfers.“Hey, Notah. It’s been an unbelievable ride with you. You first came into my life when I was 11-years-old, playing in the junior world and you came to watch me play. Our friendship has started there and never ended,” Woods said.He also praised Begay for the work he has done away from golf, especially for Native American communities.“You’ve done an amazing job. I just think more people need to know what you’ve done and how you’ve served, and you’ve given back to the tribal lands and what you have done,” Woods said.He ended the message on a personal note, thanking Begay for being there early in his golf career.“Again, thank you for coming to see me play. Thank you for getting our friendship started and I love you dude.”Golf Channel also shared Woods’ message, describing Begay as his longtime friend and former Stanford teammate.Tiger Woods made a rare appearance through a video message for longtime friend Notah Begay III at the Payne Stewart Award ceremony. While Woods focused on Begay’s work and their long friendship, fans quickly noticed his appearance and shared mixed reactions. Woods, who has stayed mostly out of public view since his March DUI arrest, is scheduled to appear in court September 8.The video was notable because Woods has kept a low profile since his March 27 crash on Jupiter Island, Florida. According to the PGA Tour, his Land Rover struck another vehicle and rolled onto its side. Authorities said Woods showed signs of impairment, while a breath test showed no alcohol in his system. He later refused a urine test.Woods faces two misdemeanor charges: DUI with property damage and refusal to submit to a lawful test. He has pleaded not guilty. Reuters reported that police found two hydrocodone pills in his possession after the crash.The New York Post reported that Woods underwent treatment in Switzerland after the arrest and has stayed away from public view since returning to the United States.His video appearance led some fans to focus less on the message and more on how he looked.“Tiger looks a shell of his former self sadly,” one X user wrote.Another posted, “What’s going on with the big cat? Looks different for sure.”A third fan added, “Geez, Tiger doesn’t look so good.”Others pushed back, saying his appearance did not necessarily mean anything was wrong.Woods’ next major public moment could come in court. articles.title: Clayton Kershaw Might Have Another Great Dodgers Career After Booth Debut
articles.summary: Los Angeles Dodgers legend Clayton Kershaw took a bold step in his broadcasting career, serving as the lead analyst in the booth of a baseball game alongside...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers legend Clayton Kershaw took a bold step in his broadcasting career, serving as the lead analyst in the booth of a baseball game alongside play-by-play guy Joe Davis.

Kershaw has served as a part-time sideline analyst for NBC on the "Sunday Night Baseball" broadcast.

However, he has now filled in for Orel Hershiser, Sportsnet LA's main partner for Davis.

It was quite a move for Kershaw, given that he just retired from baseball only months ago, but he has now given broadcasters a trial of what he could offer in the booth if need be.

Breaking down Kershaw's time in the booth

Not to bury the lede, Kershaw was stellar in the booth next to Davis. He offered a ton of great insights into pitching, relaying stories and anecdotes he'd heard and experienced.

Rather than simply resting on his knowledge of the Dodgers, Kershaw had done his homework and offered analysis on the Braves pitching staff, including starter Bryce Elder and the bullpen.

Having worked so closely with Dodgers pitchers as recently as a few months ago, Kershaw had a ton to offer on the current crop of players.

His best moment of the night came when he said that pitchers cannot be afraid of their offspeed stuff even if it bounced in the dirt a pitch before.

Pitchers need to avoid closing their options to just a fastball in 3-2 counts, and they need to be willing to throw offspeed and trust their stuff, especially since hitters expect a challenge fastball to avoid a walk.

It was a great peek into the mind of one of the best pitchers of all time, who knows a thing or two about taking the mound.

His pitching knowledge let him break down a hitter's approach and why they make certain swing decisions.

Tyler Glasnow was making his first start since May, and Kershaw offered much about what a pitcher is looking for after a long layoff.

The key difference between Kershaw and Herschier, in terms of their styles as analysts, is that Kershaw is much more tapped into modern practices and can speak to the experience of playing in the analytical era, while also bringing some of the old-school know-how Herschier offers.

This is all from the actual baseball side of things, but even as a partner to Davis, Kershaw has the personality of being a big kid who just loves the sport.

He gets giddy during big moments and isn't afraid to sound awkward or make mistakes; instead, he takes things in stride and doesn't seem to overthink stepping into an unfamiliar role.

Going forward, if Herschier ever needs to take a break or miss a game or two, Kershaw has shown to be more than capable of stepping into the booth.

SNLA will need to be careful because ESPN, NBC, or FOX will be taking note of what Kershaw can offer, and his profile as an analyst should only rise as he gets more experience.

Was his debut performance as good as his pitching? No, he was unhittable at the peak of his powers and made hitters look silly, but Kershaw established himself as a hot analyst prospect, and for a rookie, his debut was everything he could have hoped for.

articles.title: Jaguars Get Relieving Brian Thomas Jr. Injury Update Before Preseason Finale
articles.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars receiving corps battle was interesting enough as it was, but Tuesday added a whole new layer to the three-way fight between Brian Th...
articles.body:
The Jacksonville Jaguars receiving corps battle was interesting enough as it was, but Tuesday added a whole new layer to the three-way fight between Brian Thomas Jr. , Parker Washington , and Jakobi Meyers for the WR1 spot.

Brian Thomas Jr. gave Jacksonville an early scare during Tuesday's joint practice with Tampa Bay.

On the very first snap of 11-on-11 drills, Thomas blew past the Bucs' secondary to track down a 40-yard pass from Trevor Lawrence .

He completed the catch for a touchdown but landed hard on his shoulder and came up clutching the injury. Thomas stayed on the field for one more rep before Jacksonville's training staff pulled him to the sideline to get him checked, and ultimately shut him down for the rest of the day.

GettyJacksonville Jaguars HC Liam Coen updates Brian Thomas Jr's injury status.

The chaos caused instant panic, but head coach Liam Coen was already scheduled to get behind the podium to handle the situation.

Coen called the move precautionary, expecting Thomas to be ready for Week 1.

"I think he's alright. He just came down on his shoulder," the Jaguars HC said after practice, according to ESPN's Jaguars Insider Michael DiRocco.

"I think just holding him out was smart, keep him out and get him to go for Cleveland ."

The timing couldn't have been worse for Thomas Jr. Coming off a sophomore slump, Thomas was already under pressure to re-establish himself as Trevor Lawrence's go-to guy.

Missing crucial reps late in August doesn't just stall his momentum—it leaves the door ajar for Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington to outdo him heading into Week 1. It was the final week for him to make his final push to eclipse his competitors if Coen let him have some reps in the preseason finale against Green Bay.

The Jaguars are yet to decide whether they're resting their main guys. But Thomas Jr. will not, even if they do.

GettyJacksonville Jaguars HC Liam Coen updates Brian Thomas Jr's injury status, Parker Washington rejoins practice.

Another core member of Jagaur's receiving lineup, Jakobi Meyers, had a brace on his right hand after jamming it against the Carolina Panthers in joint practice last week.

Although his official injury reason remains undisclosed, Washington sat out the preseason game last week on day-to-day basis, but made progress on Tuesday with attendance in joint practice with the Bucs.

Whether he'll actually play against Tampa Bay is a question Coen is yet to answer.

With the injury, Jaguars are likely to be without Thomas as they return to joint practice with the Buccaneers on Aug. 26.

That leaves them with rookie wide receivers CJ Williams and Josh Cameron , who had an uptick in reps as the two starting pass catchers watched from the sideline.

Coen said he'd have to further evaluate their days when he watches film but credited them for blocking well in the run game.

Despite being without two of their three best receivers, Trevor Lawrence and Jacksonville's offense were able to have a strong performance on Tuesday passing the football thanks to Parker Washington and Brenton Strange .

articles.title: Bennedict Mathurin to sign with Pelicans, face Pacers in season opener
articles.summary: Bennedict Mathurin will reportedly sign a two-year contract with the Pelicans for similar money to Kelly Oubre; who should the Pacers have signed?
articles.body:
The Pacers will get to see old friend Bennedict Mathurin again in their season opener.

The Pacers ' third-leading rookie scorer in franchise history will sign a two-year, $16 million contract with the New Orleans Pelicans , ESPN's Shams Charania reported Wednesday morning. Mathurin was traded to the Clippers as part of the February deal that brought Ivica Zubac to Indiana , and the Clippers have an opportunity to match the Pelicans' offer as a restricted free agent, but Charania and Jake Fischer of the Stein Line reported that the Clippers will work to make sure the deal works out and Mathurin goes to New Orleans .

The Pacers play the Pelicans in New Orleans on Oct. 21.

Former Pacer Bennedict Mathurin through the years

The Pacers selected Mathurin with the No. 6 overall pick in the 2022 draft, making him the Pacers' highest selection since Rik Smits was taken No. 2 overall in 1988. He responded by scoring the third-most points by a rookie in the Pacers' NBA history with 16.7 per game and a total of 1,302 points. Only Clark Kellogg and Chuck Person scored more as Pacers rookies. Mathurin also became the first Pacers rookie since Smits to be named first-team All-Rookie.

In the next three-plus seasons, Mathurin struggled to connect with the high-paced, ball-movement driven offense built around All-Star point guard Tyrese Haliburton as he is more of an isolation, one-on-one scorer by nature. However, when they needed someone to put his head down and go get a bucket -- particularly someone off the bench -- Mathurin was often the answer. He averaged 16.1 points per game in nearly four seasons with the Pacers. That included 17.6 points per game in 2025-26 when he often started on a squad that was snakebit by injuries and 16.1 per game on the 2024-25 team that reached the NBA Finals. He averaged a more modest 11.0 points per game in the 2025 playoffs -- he missed the 2024 postseason with a torn labrum -- but he cracked the 20-point mark five times in those playoffs with 20 in a Game 4 win over the Knicks in the Eastern Conference Finals and 27 in a Game 3 win over the Thunder in the Finals.

The Pacers and Mathurin apparently couldn't agree on terms for a potential extension beyond his rookie-scale deal, which ended at the end of this season so he was an obvious piece to include in the Zubac trade to be able to match salary. The Pacers also sent center Isaiah Jackson and three draft picks to the Clippers including, conditionally, their 2026 first-round pick. The Pacers would have kept the selection if it landed in the top four or from 10-30, but it landed at No. 5 and the Clippers used the selection to pick Keaton Wagler .

Mathurin had struggles with the Clippers which obviously hurt his market value going into restricted free agency. He averaged 17.4 points per game in 26 games with Los Angeles , but shot just 42.6% from the floor -- worse than any of his seasons with the Pacers -- and made just 20.7% of his 3-pointers (17 of 82).

Are the Pacers better with Kelly Oubre or Bennedict Mathurin ?

The Pacers ended up signing a wing to effectively replace Mathurin for about the same money, giving Kelly Oubre Jr. $17 million over two years. Oubre might not have Mathurin's scoring potential and he's 30 while Mathurin just turned 24 in June.

However, the 6-8 Oubre gives the Pacers' more positional versatility than the 6-5 Mathurin. He's a much more accomplished defender and still a very good scorer. Over 11 seasons, he's averaged 13.3 points per game and averaged at least 14 per game in each of the last eight seasons with a high-water mark of 20.3 in 2022-23. He's also averaged at least 1.0 steals per game in each of the last nine seasons and with a 7-foot wingspan, he can guard any position from point guard to power forward. Mathurin may have more ability to create offense for himself and others, but Oubre can score off the bounce, from outside and in transition and can make plays on the defensive end that create offense.

articles.title: Ai Ogura out of Aragon GP following Japan crash that left him in need of surgery
articles.summary: Ogura crashed while training in Japan and reportedly injured his hand, which will rule him out of Motorland this weekend and will require him to undergo surg...
articles.body:
Ai Ogura 's bad run continues. The second-placed rider in the MotoGP standings has arrived back from Japan with a hand injury that will rule him out of the Aragon Grand Prix and compromises his fight for the world championship.

In a statement issued by the American Trackhouse team, it confirmed that Ogura suffered a hand injury and is withdrawing from the Aragon race. It confirmed that Aprilia test rider Lorenzo Savadori will be his replacement at Motorland on 30 August.

"Team SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP's number 79 rider suffered an injury to his left hand during training in Japan. Upon his arrival in Europe, he was diagnosed with a fracture near the left thumb that requires surgery, which will be performed this Thursday," it reports.

"The team welcomes Lorenzo Savadori, number 32, who will replace him at this race in Aragon. We wish Ai a speedy recovery and thank Lorenzo for his willingness to replace him at such short notice."

Ogura moved to Japan in order to be close to his family and friends, and in conditions where he could train on track with production bikes and go fishing, his two great passions. However, a crash while he was riding at a track near Tokyo has dealt the rider a bad blow.

It comes after he lost a good handful of points in the championship standings following a crash last Sunday at Silverstone. He now sits third, just 37 points behind leader Jorge Martin .

Now, with his absence in Aragon confirmed, the Japanese rider could take an important step backwards in the championship fight.

articles.title: These 6 Ohio players landed on USA TODAY's college football top 100
articles.summary: Five Buckeyes and one Cincinnati Bearcat made USA TODAY's preseason top 100. Here's where they ranked and why they made the list.
articles.body:
Ohio college football programs are well represented in a new ranking that highlights some of the nation's best.

Six players from Ohio-based programs made USA TODAY's top 100 college football players entering the 2026 season, including Buckeyes star Jeremiah Smith, who claimed the No. 1 spot overall.

The rankings were based on past production, future projections and NFL draft stock. Here's where the Ohio-based players landed.

Five of the six Ohio-based players suit up for Ohio State, while Cincinnati lineman Evan Tengesdahl is the lone Bearcat included in the rankings.

USA TODAY ranked Tengesdahl No. 100 after a standout season in which he did not allow a sack in pass protection and earned the highest run-blocking grade among Power Four guards from Pro Football Focus.

The publication noted that offensive guards rarely appear on top-100 player lists, making Tengesdahl's inclusion notable for Cincinnati. The senior from Dayton started all 13 games last season after seeing action in 11 games during his sophomore season.

97. Kenyatta Jackson Jr., DE, Ohio State

Jackson Jr. is a key piece of Ohio State's defensive line heading into the 2026 season. He is the unit's only returning starter after leading the Buckeyes with 6.5 sacks last season.

Jackson Jr. started all 14 games last year and stepped up with 28 total tackles, including 11.5 tackles for loss. With his experience, Jackson is in line to take on a larger leadership role while anchoring Ohio State's pass rush.

Free safety Terry Moore, who transferred from Duke also made the list for the Buckeyes. Moore has flown under the radar for a transfer who was as heavily billed as any of the Buckeyes' pickups from January.

Moore returned to action with Ohio State after missing last season at Duke with a torn ACL and has spent the spring working back into form. He had four interceptions and five pass breakups in 2024, when he was recognized as a second-team All-American by the Action Network.

articles.title: Four Rebels featured in the ESPN Top 100 players for 2026

articles.body:
Preseason rankings for any kind list are really just there to generate conversation and excitement as you await the start of play. This list is particularly exciting for Ole Miss fans because not only do the Rebels feature four players on this list, but they have two in the top 10.

Based on my research, Laremy Tunsil is the only player since 2000 to be named in the top 10 of a top 100 preseason list when he was listed at #9 in 2015. This year's team having two, is special stuff.

So I pulled from ESPN, On3, USA Today and CBS (top 150) to take a look at how our best players are viewed around the country.

The On3 outlier really skews his average ranking and I need to find out what they are drinking because I want to avoid it. Chambliss truly is tough to get a real gauge on because he came out of nowhere and the coaching staff that vaulted him to stardom is gone. However, those old coaches didn't make the throws, he did. He's electric and if he plays like he did last year and then improves, he's the best quarterback in the country.

If he looks anything like he did last season, he's easily the best running back in college football. From pass blocking to break away speed, he's the total package. Lacy has the potential to walk away holding almost every rushing record possible at Ole Miss by season's end.

Seems to me Echoles is essentially a unanimous top 30 player entering the college football season and CBS is just slow to the party. I get that he may not be the most physically imposing presence, but analytics and game tape both point towards his dominance. Maybe CBS just made a mistake.

I don't really think it's much of a question that Perkins is a top 100 talent in college football. He is undersized to be an EDGE but doesn't have the traditional linebacker skillset. Maybe his production doesn't always scream top 100. The dude's a freak and a crucial part of an SEC defense.

A surprise entry to a top preseason list. I believe he is going to surprise a lot of people. He can make the difficult catches and he does it often. He's not the traditional WR1 type mold and he was battling Stribling, Wallace, Wright and Lee for targets last year. So while he may not make the preseason lists, he will have all the opportunity to be on the post season lists.

The Rebels ended up tied for 9th with Miami and Oklahoma for most players on the ESPN top 100 list. Oregon led the way with eight, followed by Georgia, Texas and Indiana with seven each. Ohio State was alone in fifth with six and Notre Dame, Alabama and LSU each had five.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Wide Receiver Scouting Reports: A preview of some of the WR profiles in the Yahoo Fantasy Ultra Playbook
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Joel Smyth gives a sneak peek at some of his WR profiles, available in the Yahoo Fantasy Ultra Playbook.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL season is fast approaching and the Yahoo Fantasy Ultra Playbook has everything you need to know to before your draft, giving you the tools and analysis to crush the competition. Among that analysis is Joel Smyth's WR player profiles. Below is a sneak peek of some of the 25+ wideout profiles in the Ultra Playbook, including a ceiling and risk meter for each. If you subscribe to Ultra, there are nearly 150 player profiles to digest.

Ceiling: If things fall in their favor, how big can they hit in 2026?

Risk: A subjective ranking based on injuries, surrounding injuries, coaching changes, how proven a player is, age, and other factors that bring on uncertainty.

In a small-to-medium sample size, Burden was a fantasy WR1 as a rookie on a per-play basis. He is all but guaranteed to see a major increase in said snaps with DJ Moore out of the picture, making the volume uptick less of a prediction and more so expected. His connection with Caleb Williams, especially considering he was a rookie, was tremendous, with a stark increase in stats such as targeted passer rating and catchable target rate downfield compared to his QB's average. As this young core grows in an already successful offense, Burden's playmaking ability could make him the first of many options. A groin injury in camp is unfortunate, but he should be available to play in Week 1, just with a little more risk.

Over 40% of Round 1 WRs in the last decade have finished top-36 in fantasy as a rookie. Concepcion may have a tougher path in Cleveland, but the talent can make it worth a stab in the last round of your drafts. KC was unbelievable as a 19-year-old freshman in college and may be used as an all-around threat as a rookie in the NFL, similar to his season at Texas A&M. If there is a surprise from the Browns' QB room, Concepcion can be the biggest benefactor.

Josh Downs' potential breakout season basically all comes down to him playing in more than just three-receiver sets. In 2025, 81% of Downs' targets came on routes from the slot, the highest in the NFL. Through his young career, he's never played a significant amount when the slot WR is taken off the field for a second TE, severely limiting his impact in fantasy. He's talented, but needs to be on the field more. In games with 70%+ of the snaps in his career, he becomes a usable PPR piece with over 13 PPG. The departure of Michael Pittman Jr. will open that potential up in 2026, especially if Alec Pierce isn't 100% prior to Week 1. Keenan Allen's addition is scary for target competition, but he isn't expected to replace Downs in 2-WR sets, which is the most important factor.

After 12 years in Tampa Bay, Evans finds himself with Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy in an attempt for one more top fantasy season. The vet has missed 17 of his last 34 games, with the hamstring injuries being the main red flag in his profile. Evans was still commanding elite volume when healthy last season and can take full advantage of a QB who currently has a higher yards per attempt than any QB in the modern era. The early talk has him shining as the team's WR1, as a combination of red-zone work and the 49ers top-10 offense is the dream for those buying in on Evans. Not many receivers continue producing at 33 years old, but not many receivers show the longevity he has through 12 seasons.

Zay Flowers was a borderline fantasy WR1 last season with Lamar Jackson, and is being drafted like it. It's been a steady growth through three career seasons and 2026 looks bright for his first WR1 season. Declan Doyle will be the X-factor. Todd Monken was good in Baltimore as the play-caller, but the former Bears OC will now get a shot at calling plays, providing some hope and potential that the passing volume won't rank 32nd, as it did in 2025. If Doyle brings an offense similar to Chicago's, Flowers can benefit in a big way after a season where his receiving efficiency rivaled some of the best in the league. If red-zone volume comes with it, watch out.

Even as the top WR on the team with the seventh-most receiving fantasy points, Harrison failed to crack the top 36 receivers. There's some positives to look at — his usage in the red zone, his good numbers in the short stint when healthy with Jacoby Brissett and an expanded route tree. Although he hasn't lived up to lofty expectations early in his career, it doesn't mean he won't have the classic Year 3 WR breakout. His path just may be harder than most. A new coaching staff could utilize him closer to his Ohio State role, which would help, but he'd still be competing along three other talented receiving threats with Brissett as the top QB option.

Everything seems to be changing for the better for McLaurin this offseason. After a throwaway season full of injuries to himself and his QB, Washington changes offensive coaching and philosophy away from the Kliff Kingsbury offense. McLaurin moves from a static role as the "left" WR to more versatile movement around the formation. The addition of Stefon Diggs limits his WR1 volume potential, but isn't a total killer for his fantasy value. If the Commanders end up playing more under center and play action as they say they will, the Commanders WR1 can be set up for a career year.

McMillan had flaws in his rookie season, but it didn't stop him from being a top-20 fantasy WR immediately. The 2025 eighth overall selection in the NFL Draft can break out in an even bigger way in Year 2. A surprisingly accurate connection downfield with QB Bryce Young can lead to some big weeks, particularly when Carolina throws so much in the red zone. The drops and contested catches should start to rebound, closer to his college numbers, providing him plenty of room to grow on top of an already good rookie outing.

articles.title: Scottie Scheffler gives fresh health update after hand, foot and mouth disease diagnosis
articles.summary: Scottie Scheffler struggled with the viral infection at last week’s BMW Championship
articles.body:
World number one Scottie Scheffler has confirmed he is fit and ready to challenge for a second FedExCup title in Atlanta this weekend, having overcome a bout of hand, foot and mouth disease.

The condition, which leads to blister outbreaks, hampered the American during the BMW Championship last week. According to NHS guidance, the viral infection usually clears up by itself within 7-10 days.

Despite his physical struggles, Scheffler managed to record a 12th-place finish in the event and now competes for the $10 million top prize for winning the play-off series at the season-closing Tour Championship at East Lake.

"I'm good," the American told reporters at a press conference. "I'd say I'm at 95 per cent.

"The only thing maybe is still just a couple of sores in my throat but other than that I feel really good."

Scheffler is the favourite heading into the 30-man event, where the victor will be crowned the overall PGA Tour champion.

Scheffler won the opening play-off tournament at the FedEx St Jude Championship a fortnight ago, while Wyndham Clark held off a late fightback from Rory McIlroy to triumph in last week's BMW Championship. Tommy Fleetwood enters the tournament as defending champion.

On Tuesday, the PGA Tour announced that the championship is set to be revamped from 2028 and will instead be played using a two-week match play format. A round-robin stage will take place in the opening week, followed by knockout rounds on a different course the following week.

Scheffler appeared to have mixed feelings about the prospective concept.

"I think it's something people have been craving, especially the fans. To change the format we have now with more matches on the course could be interesting and fun," he said.

"It's a little bit hard for me to wrap my head around the group play – when I show up at a tournament I love to be able to compete and give myself a chance to win.

"To have a full week where there's not a winner is a bit unusual for me but I think it's fun, it's an interesting new way to finish the year."

articles.title: Robot Tops Usain Bolt Track Record With Historic 100m Time at World Humanoid Games
articles.summary: Three humanoid robots have officially topped Usain Bolt's world record in the 100-meter race...again.
articles.body:
Three humanoid robots have officially topped Usain Bolt's world record in the 100-meter race...again.

A robotic sprinter ran the 100 meters in 8.84 seconds on Wednesday at the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, according to the Associated Press .

The feat was accomplished the day after other robots clocked 100-meter times of 8.86 seconds and 9.39 seconds earlier in the Games, per the AP.

New Grand Theft Auto game leaks confirmed

Bolt set the human 100-meter world record with a 9.58-second run in 2009 during the World Athletics Championship in Berlin.

The record robot runs were recorded by the Tiangong Ultra model developed by the Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics, according to the AP.

The same model of robot won the world's first humanoid half marathon in April 2025 by completing the 13-mile route in two hours and 40 minutes.

Technology had advanced by this April to the point a robot designed by the Chinese smartphone maker Honor beat the human world record by running a half marathon in 50 minutes and 26 seconds.

The World Humanoid Robot Games, which runs through Wednesday in Beijing, also features robots competing in sports like football and table tennis as well as tasks like firefighting.

articles.title: Blues Prospect Matthew Mayich Hospitalized After Collapsing During ASU  Workout
articles.summary: St. Louis Blues prospect and Arizona State sophomore Matthew Mayich is continuing to undergo medical treatment after collapsing and being hospitalized following an outdoor workout last Thursday.
articles.body:
St. Louis Blues prospect and Arizona State sophomore Matthew Mayich is continuing to undergo medical treatment after collapsing and being hospitalized following an outdoor workout last Thursday.

Blues president of hockey operations Doug Armstrong announced the news in a Wednesday statement in which he shared prayers for Mayich's "comfort and recovery."

The USHL and OHL also shared prayers for Mayich's recovery in Wednesday statements.

"Our thoughts are with Matthew, his parents John and Christina and the entire Mayich family," said OHL commissioner Bryan Crawford said in a statement . "Matthew spent four seasons in our league and earned the respect of everyone he played with and against. The entire Ontario Hockey League is thinking of him and pulling for him, and we are keeping his family close in our thoughts."

Victoria Beara, cousin of Mayich and wife of the Buffalo Sabres' Owen Power, spoke in a virtual prayer service held in Mayich's honor Tuesday, per the Arizona Republic's Rey Covarrubias Jr. and Robert Anglen .

Mayich, 21, was drafted by the Blues in 2023. After four seasons in the OHL, he spent his freshman NCAA season with Clarkson before transferring to ASU.

ASU vice president of media relations Chris Fiscus told The Athletic's Katie Strang and Jeremy Rutherford one of the team's student-athletes remained hospitalized as of Tuesday.

"The university is reviewing the circumstances surrounding the workout," Fiscus told Strang and Rutherford.

According to Strang and Rutherford, "Fiscus declined to answer if the team sanctioned the workout."

Mayich, a sixth-round NHL draft pick who has yet to sign with the Blues, contributed 15 points (seven goals, eight assists) in 34 games on Clarkson's blue line last season.

He is part of a 10-person incoming transfer class that marked the largest group of DI signees in the country.

articles.title: Atlanta NHL comeback bid takes major step with new arena progress
articles.summary: Alpharetta's city council narrowly approved redeveloping North Point Mall into a massive entertainment district with a 20,000-seat NHL-ready arena.
articles.body: There's a lot of buzz around the NHL about the league bringing in 33rd and 34th franchises, and one of those looks set to head to either Austin or Houston. The leader in the clubhouse for the other is Atlanta (yes, again), and one of the two groups looking to bring a team to town hit a big milestone this week. The city council in Alpharetta, Georgia, a northern Atlanta suburb, voted 4-3 to approve the redevelopment of the North Point Mall into a mixed-use entertainment district featuring a very large arena capable of being home to an NHL team. SACRAMENTO MAKES ITS CASE AS MLB'S NEXT EXPANSION CITY, CALLING ITSELF A MARKET TOO BIG TO IGNORE The proposal was led by real estate and placemaking firm Jamestown for the site owner, New York Life, and in partnership with real estate developer Machete Group, which specializes in this kind of project. "We are thrilled to have achieved this significant milestone and grateful to the City of Alpharetta, its elected officials, staff, and the community for their thorough review and support of our vision for North Point’s future," Chief Investment Officer at Jamestown Tim Perry said in a statement. "This approval reflects the City’s confidence in the transformative opportunity of the project and in Jamestown’s ability to bring this vision to life. It also positions North Point to become a regional, year-round destination for professional sports, entertainment, and mixed-use experiences, while bringing substantial investment, economic impact, and community benefit." The plan is for the site to be home to a 20,000-seat arena, which would make it the second-biggest in the league behind only Montreal's Bell Centre. The site would also be home to a 4,000-seat music hall and performing arts center, a 2,000-seat community hockey rink, a 1,100-seat movie theater, a 35,000-square-foot hotel conference center, and hundreds of rooms across two hotel buildings. WWE SURVIVOR SERIES: WARGAMES HEADS TO HOUSTON IN NOVEMBER Interestingly, this is one of two groups looking to build an NHL venue in the area. Another project is being proposed in Forsyth County, just seven miles away, according to FOX 5 Atlanta. The NHL previously had a presence in Atlanta from 1972 to 1980 with the Atlanta Flames before they moved to Calgary, and then again from 1999 to 2011 with the Atlanta Thrashers before they moved to Winnipeg and became the current version of the Jets. articles.title: Hot take alert: ESPN getting rid of 'BottomLine' score ticker is a travesty, not a reason to celebrate
articles.summary: ESPN's decision to remove the "BottomLine" score ticker from college football broadcasts is drawing praise from fans, but not everyone agrees.
articles.body: In case you missed the news, ESPN is getting rid of its "BottomLine" score ticker during college football broadcasts this coming season. As Yahoo Sports reports, the network is trying to streamline the college football viewer experience for fans, and will remove the ticker from all broadcasts of the sport across its different channels. ESPN has already gotten rid of the "BottomLine" during other live broadcasts such as the College Football Playoff and NBA postseason games. As soon as I heard this news, I immediately went to social media to see what the reaction would be. Surely, everyone felt the same way as I did, right? That is to say, this is a horrible move by ESPN and just another way the network is taking away what we love little by little in a sort of "frog in the boiling pot of water" way. But, much to my surprise and chagrin, the move is being widely lauded by fans across all of social media. The vast majority of people weighing in on the removal of the "BottomLine" are doing so in support of the decision. Some fans say it's a needless distraction, while others say they can just check their phones for the scores and call anyone who flinches at this announcement a "grandpa" or a "boomer." THESE ONCE-ANNUAL COLLEGE RIVALRIES USED TO DEFINE COLLEGE FOOTBALL AND NEED TO MAKE A COMEBACK ASAP If I may be so bold, these people are missing the point so badly they couldn't find it with a telescope. This is just another example of ESPN bastardizing something that we grew up with and loved deeply: college football. Sure, anyone can open up their phone and see that Arkansas is covering the spread against LSU, but that takes all the fun out of it. There's nothing more electric than watching a game and seeing the ticker light up with the words "UPSET ALERT" in big, bold letters at the bottom of the screen. Besides, who wants to be on their phones all game long anyway? And anyone calling a ticker that takes up roughly 8% of their television screen is either being insanely disingenuous or has some serious attention span issues. Are your brains so fried that a ticker distracts you from watching the greatest sport on earth every Saturday? This is coming from the same people that need to have the subtitles on during their stupid Netflix documentaries, though, so it's all starting to make sense. SEC FOOTBALL DOING AWAY WITH 'CUPCAKE WEEKEND' MEANS THE DEATH OF ANOTHER COLLEGE FOOTBALL TRADITION Taking away the "BottomLine" ticker is just another shot in the crotch to that all-important "tradition" that makes college football king. It will be hilarious to see these same people that are celebrating in the streets about the demise of the "BottomLine" talk about it with reverence a few decades from now. "Man, they used to have this ticker that would tell you all the scores at the bottom of the screen. Can't believe they got rid of it." These are also the same people that whine about ESPN doing away with the old College Football Saturday theme song and wax poetically about the scorebug from 15 years ago, so I just know they'll come around to pretending they used to care about the "BottomLine." articles.title: PC28: Luke Littler beaten by Brendan Dolan in semi-finals
articles.summary: Luke Littler's hopes of qualifying for the Players Championship finals suffers another setback as he is beaten by Brendan Dolan in the semi-finals of PC28 in Leicester.
articles.body:
Luke Littler's hopes of qualifying for the Players Championship finals suffered another setback as he was beaten by Brendan Dolan in the semi-finals of PC28 in Leicester.

The world champion went a step further than he managed at Tuesday's PC27, but still fell short of the title, which was won by fellow Englishman Luke Humphries with an 8-6 victory over Dolan.

"Luke has been by far the best player in the last 18 months and he deserves the world number one spot," said world number two Humphries after his victory.

"He's won everything and I am going to be the only one who's trying to stop him.

"I want to go on and win a major this year. I don't want him to have a clean sweep - as much as everyone would love to see it."

Littler, meanwhile, climbed from 141st to 125th in the order of merit with prize money of £10,500 and posted on Instagram: "We are so on the move."

But the semi-final defeat leaves the world number one with work to do in the race to reach November's finals in his attempt to complete the calendar sweep of ranking events in 2026.

Only the top 64 players in the Players Championship qualify for Minehead.

And Littler, who skipped the first 26 events on the circuit, is currently £16,750 behind 64th-placed Shane McGuirk.

On Wednesday, the 19-year-old beat Benjamin Pratnemer, Martin Schindler and Krzysztof Ratajski to reach the final four, where he was denied by Northern Irishman Dolan.

The world number one has largely skipped the floor events this year in an effort to manage his schedule.

With the projected cutoff expected to exceed £30,000 after all 34 events, and only six events remaining, Littler might travel to Den Bosch next month to boost his hopes of reaching the finals.

He has previously stated his intention to only feature in the UK events, and the two in Leicester on 4 and 5 November complete the qualification stage.

Littler was defeated by Jermaine Wattimena in the quarter-finals of PC27 on Tuesday.

articles.summary: Luke Humphries wins on the second day of Players Championship action in Leicester after 8-6 victory over Brendan Dolan, who had beaten Luke Littler in semi-final; Littler, who made his first two appearances of 2026's series this week, with work to do if he is to make November finals.
articles.body:
Humphries, who reclaimed the world No 2 position in the PDC rankings from Gian van Veen during the course of the day, beat Ireland's Dolan 8-6 to win PC28 for his first title in the series since PC17 in May, also held at the Mattioli Arena.

Dolan had defeated Luke Littler 7-4 in their semi-final to deny the world No 1 a blockbuster meeting with Humphries.

Humphries beat Mike De Decker 7-4 in his semi-final, two rounds after surviving six match darts against Danny Noppert to win that match 6-5.

Littler was making just his second Players Championship appearance of the season after a quarter-final defeat to eventual PC27 winner Jermaine Wattimena on Tuesday.

Having sat out the first 26 Players Championship events this year, Littler is aiming to make the top 64 on the Order of Merit over the tournaments that remain to qualify for the finals in Minehead in November amid his bid for a historic clean sweep of PDC major titles this season.

A quarter-final and semi-final appearance in Leicester mean he now sits in 125th place in the Order of Merit, £16,750 behind 64th place. Six events remain before the finals with Littler needing to play, and play well, in further events if he is to have a chance of making up the further ground required to qualify.

He still needs to win the World Series, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals this season in order to achieve something no one has ever managed in the sport.

The World Series event takes place in Amsterdam on September 17-20 and finishes two days before the next Players Championship double header gets under way in Den Bosch, by which time Littler will know whether or not he remains on course for the clean sweep.

Littler has won every major title on the PDC circuit so far in 2026 - the World Championship, Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.

On Wednesday in Leicester, Littler made light work of Stephen Rosney in the first round, winning 6-4, before his day nearly ended in the next round as he survived six match darts against world number 107 Benjamin Pratnemer, eventually winning a final-leg decider.

Quickfire wins against Martin Schindler, Andy Boulton and Krzysztof Ratajski sent him through to the last four, but Dolan was too good for him

'I don't want him to have the clean sweep' - Humphries keen to deny Littler major history

Humphries returned to competitive action this week for the first time since his shock round-one exit to Cameron Menzies in the World Matchplay on July 20.

He lost 6-3 Cam Crabtree in Tuesday's first round in Leicester but returned on Wednesday to win all seven of his matches.

Humphries was only playing in his ninth such floor event the year, although he has now won three times after victories at PC4 and PC17.

He sits 13th in the standings and with £52,000 won so far is effectively assured of featuring in Minehead.

"To be honest, I know it sounds crazy being one of the best players in the world, I just came here for a bit of practice. Just to get myself in and feel normal again," said Humphries.

"I've only played that matchplay in two months so I just had to get myself back into it. I didn't want to go straight in to the Euro Tour this weekend with no practice.

"Obviously that's the reason I was here but once you get to the latter stages you're like 'right, ok, you can go on and win this now'. I must admit, I didn't really think I'd go on and win one this week because of the lack of practice, but I've had two good days, a lot of practice and hopefully in the next couple of weeks or couple pf months I can keep building on that.

"I'm going to get back on the practice board at home as much as I can now and I'm going to dedicate the rest of the year to trying to be my best and trying to push Luke - and not just Luke, but everyone else because I want to stay at No 2. Whether that happens or not, I'm going to fight for it because I'm going to try my best.

Asked whether the win would give him an extra boost heading to the Hungarian Darts Trophy this weekend, Humphries replied: "One hundred per cent. It's good confidence because I didn't really play my best but I still managed to go on and win.

"I don't think a lot of people have played their best these last two days, to be fair. It's been funny. Luke hasn't played his best either. Had a couple of good runs, he won't care.

"Obviously, I'm kind of just looking about trying to get a bit of practice and I've done that so for me now it's about putting in the dedication for the rest of the year because I want to go on and win a major.

"I don't want him to have the clean sweep. As much as everyone would love to see it, I'd love to win one this year and go to the Worlds in a bit of confidence.

"So this will do me good and I'm going to enjoy tonight and enjoy the moment."

articles.title: Seattle Seahawks place UCLA alum Jake Bobo on season-ending IR
articles.summary: Former UCLA Bruin wide receiver Jake Bobo will miss the entire 2026 season after suffering a torn ACL.
articles.body:
The NFL season is not even under way yet but one former UCLA Bruin is already out for the season with Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jake Bobo tearing his ACL in a joint practice against the Tennessee Titans last week.

Bobo is fresh off of a Super Bowl victory with the Seahawks but he won't be with the team to defend their title, with Seattle placing the wideout on season-ending injured reserve.

Even when healthy, Bobo wasn't a huge part of the Seahawks' offense. Last season, Bobo caught two passes during the regular season but he did add another two catches, including a touchdown in the playoffs for Seattle.

Seahawks Wire writer Kole Musgrove wrote about Bobo's injury on Sunday.

"Turns out the worst fears were absolutely realized. ESPN's Adam Schefter and Brady Henderson reported on Saturday that Jake Bobo 's leg injury was serious enough to land him on the season-ending Injured Reserve (IR) list. This will sadly end Bobo's title defense campaign before it gets a chance to begin," Musgrove said. "The loss of Bobo will test Seattle's wide receiver depth, as well as their special teams - where they were the best in the NFL last season."

Bobo has played all three seasons, all with the Seahawks, since leaving the college game. Bobo played four seasons with Duke before closing out his NCAA career with one season with the Bruins . In his one season with UCLA , Bobo hauled in 57 receptions for a career-best 817 yards and seven touchdowns.

articles.title: Arsenal Identify This Juventus Winger As A Target: What Will He Bring To North London?
articles.summary: In a recent report, The Independent stated that Arsenal have identified Juventus winger Kenan Yildiz as a target. It has been claimed that the Gunners consid...
articles.body:
In a recent report , The Independent stated that Arsenal have identified Juventus winger Kenan Yildiz as a target. It has been claimed that the Gunners consider the Turkish talent as an option if they fail to sign Atletico Madrid 's Julian Alvarez this month.

Yildiz enjoyed an excellent run of form at the Turin club in the previous campaign when he produced a series of impressive displays for them on the left flank. The 21-year-old registered 11 goals and grabbed ten assists in 47 appearances for Juventus last season across all competitions.

The Turkish talent is currently among the most talented wide players in Serie A . Hence, it is no surprise that the Gunners are eager to snap him up in this transfer window.

His current deal at the Allianz Stadium will run out in the summer of 2030, which could make it tough for Arsenal to land him on a cut-price deal this month.

FROSINONE, ITALY – AUGUST 23: Kenan Yildiz of Juventus FC looks dejected during the Serie A match between Frosinone Calcio and Juventus at Stadio Benito Stirpe on August 23, 2026 in Frosinone, Italy. (Photo by Giuseppe Bellini/Getty Images)

What Will Yildiz Add To Arsenal Boss Mikel Arteta's Side?

Yildiz is a good dribbler with the ball at his feet and can make some dangerous runs with it out on the left wing. He has the vision to engineer some decent chances for his teammates in the final third.

The Turkish talent can shoot the ball with power from long range and can contribute by scoring and creating his fair share of goals from the wide areas. Yildiz mainly functions as a left-winger but can also operate as a right-sided wide player or as a striker if asked to do so. However, there are some concerns over whether he can cope with the physical side and high intensity of the Premier League if the Gunners manage to get a deal done for him this month.

We can expect Yildiz to bring more quality and depth to Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta's attack. He has what it takes to fight for a regular starting spot at the Emirates Stadium in the coming years.

At 21, Yildiz has a bright future ahead of him and would be a great signing for the Gunners in the long run. However, Arteta has to give him some time to adjust to life in the English capital before he can get the best out of him.

articles.title: Another LIV Vendor Ramps Up Legal Fight As Layoffs Hit League
articles.summary: Deltatre, a sports technology service provider, is suing LIV.
articles.body:
Another former LIV Golf vendor is waging a legal fight with the league over missed payments, as LIV's future is in limbo .

Deltatre, a sports technology service provider that began working with LIV during its 2025 season, requested a motion for summary judgment in New York State Supreme Court earlier this month—effectively asking for a judge to rule in its favor without needing further court proceedings. The company filed a breach-of-contract lawsuit against LIV with the court on May 22, which had not been previously reported. Deltatre said at the time that LIV owed it $858,548.15. With additional costs from interest and attorneys' fees, that total has risen to approximately $935,000, a source with knowledge of the legal proceedings told Front Office Sports .

"LIV does not deny the contracts, the services, its acceptance of those services, or its receipt of the invoices or its failure to object to them," Deltatre wrote in its latest filing on Aug. 13. "It admits each of those facts. That leaves a straightforward question for this motion: whether a customer that accepted the contracted-for services, retained the resulting invoices without objection, approved the invoices for payment, and nevertheless left $858,548.15 unpaid as of the date of the filing of this action may avoid judgment through generalized affirmative defenses unsupported by the factual record. It may not."

Deltatre is not the only vendor to sue LIV. Fresh Tape Media, which produced LIV's preseason media days event in January, is suing the league for more than $1.23 million in missed payments and interest. Mobii Systems Group Limited, a former technology partner of LIV, has also sued the league for more than $1.1 million for breach of contract, unpaid invoices, and interest. Other vendors and contractors have told FOS they are also owed money by the league.

LIV CEO Scott O'Neil was asked about the status of unpaid vendors last week ahead of LIV's season finale in Indianapolis. "What I would say to them is we're doing everything we can to make sure we can do right by them and the work they committed," O'Neil said. "And I hope we can."

LIV's financial issues go beyond unpaid invoices.

LIV announced on Wednesday that it is laying off staff and scaling back its operations now that the Saudi PIF is no longer funding the league. The league is in talks with BC Partners Credit over a new funding deal .

"The funding commitment announced by PIF earlier this year will reach its conclusion," a LIV spokesperson said in a statement Wednesday to FOS . "As a result, we are scaling back operations as we transition to the next chapter of LIV Golf and work toward making LIV 2.0 a reality. This week, we informed many of our colleagues that their employment under LIV 1.0 will end in the first week of September. We are grateful to our employees for their hard work and dedication in building LIV Golf, and we remain committed to supporting those affected through this transition."

The layoffs were not unexpected given LIV's uncertain future, and employees could have additional opportunities with LIV if the league lives on.

While there is no public deadline for LIV to finalize a deal with BC Partners, Sept. 1 has been floating among golf industry sources as a working deadline—one that may be necessary to meet in order to plan a 2027 schedule.

The jamboree is split into two sessions with JV and C teams beginning their scrimmages at 5:30 p.m. The varsity jamboree is set to start immediately after at 7 p.m.

Each team will get to play their offensive and defensive squads against their opponents and will face each team throughout the event. The jamboree will act as a way for players and coaches alike to get a feel for playing against other teams ahead of their regular season games.

"I think it just kind of gives that little taste of competition against that other team, where then you can't wait to play that next game," said Tigers head coach Patrick Mitchell after last years jamboree.

Former Knight Shea Stevenson spoke highly of the benefits they found in last years jamboree as they headed into the 2025 season.

"I think (the jamboree) prepares us pretty well," said Stevenson. "It kind of gives us a preview of what our team really is, and I think we're going to excel in our first game."

articles.title: Judge issues mixed rulings after Gibbs, Gabehart, Spire hearing
articles.summary: A trial is set to begin on February 1 for everything on the merits
articles.body:
Following a two-hour hearing on Wednesday at the Charles R. Jonas Federal Building, Judge Susan C. Rodriguez issued rulings on the motions from Joe Gibbs Racing to dismiss countersuits from Spire Motorsports and Chris Gabehart .

As is typical in such litigation, a lawsuit is followed by a countersuit of some kind, and this was no different with the defendants making a variety of counterclaims on their own.

Joe Gibbs Racing sued Gabehart, who worked at the organization from 2012 to 2025 as an engineer, crew chief and competition director, for the misappropriation of trade secrets for the benefits of his new employer, Spire .

In response, Spire sued JGR over an 'oral agreement,' 'de facto agreement' and 'unjust enrichment' over an implied deal that saw Spire release championship-winning car chief Robert 'Cheddar' Smith from his contract so he could leave for Gibbs' No. 54 team, driven by Ty Gibbs, the grandson of team owner Joe Gibbs.

In exchange, Spire claim Gibbs agreed to release an equivalent competition level employee to join Spire or pay $100,000 for Smith's services. Smith was released and joined JGR but Spire never received a commensurate employee or payment.

Gabehart also sued Joe Gibbs Racing under the claims that his longtime employer actually breached its contract with him, and not vice versa, withholding wages and the finality of their agreement in the efforts to prevent him from working elsewhere.

Gabehart also filed a lawsuit alleging that Joe Gibbs Racing's attorneys at the Parker Poe firm broke attorney-client privilege while conducting a digital forensic analysis of the competition director's company issued devices after his departure.

JGR had hired a private investigator to follow Gabehart and was under the conviction that he was preparing to leave for Spire while in possession of propriety business and competition data.

Much of that is to be determined during the remaining fact discovery phase, summary judgement and a trial that is scheduled for February 1.

On Wednesday, Judge Rodriguez effectively denied Joe Gibbs Racing's motion to dismiss the countersuit from Spire Motorsports regarding Cheddar Smith.

This doesn't mean that the judge was ruling on the merits of the legal arguments, but rather that there is plausible claims for relief if the allegations were true, and that the matter can proceed forward.

In other words, the counterclaims cannot be reasonably or legally superfluous, and these were not.

"On the merits, we're not there yet," Rodriguez told all parties while reading her decisions.

JGR attorney Sarah Hutchins argued that any agreement between the two teams was nebulous since the two parties never crafted a contract. She also argued that there was nothing tangible to indicate that JGR had substantially benefitted from hiring Smith.

Spire attorney Joshua D. Davey responded that the No. 54 team has won twice this season and sits third in the standings after Ty Gibbs missed the Cup Series playoffs last year. That happened after Spire allowed Smith, the 2014 championship-winning car chief, out of his no-compete contract.

"I'm puzzled by the argument that there was no benefit to JGR," said Davey. "JGR needed a car chief. They got one."

Judge Rodriguez did not seem moved by the JGR argument either.

"This whole lawsuit is about non-competes and (how) they're valuable, right?" Rodriguez said. "They're not waived lightly."

Regarding the countersuit from Gabehart, Judge Rodriguez granted in part and denied in part Joe Gibbs Racing's motions to dismiss. She is allowing Gabehart's countersuit on breach of contract, a breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing and the North Carolina Wage and Hour Act to continue forward.

Joe Gibbs Racing stopped paying Gabehart's wages in November before it issued 'a for cause' termination letter in February after he signed with Spire. Gabehart is arguing in court that the 18-month non-compete agreement was overly broad and not enforceable

On the other hand, Rodriguez granted the motion to dismiss on Gabehart's claims that JGR violated the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, North Carolina's Computer Trespass Act and unfair and deceptive trade practices law.

"I'm just not sure you've got anything plausible here," Rodriguez told Davis during the hearing.

This was said during an argument in which Davis stated that JGR exceeded its authority to inspect Gabehart's accounts and computer. Davis was adamant that the legal standard was recognizing that certain communications were privileged and not opening them.

The devices were owned by Joe Gibbs Racing and provided to Gabehart for his use as an employee. In other words, for Davis to argue that JGR's attorneys didn't have the authority to access their own devices didn't make a lot of legal sense to the judge.

"If I were to adopt this, I would be making a new law here," she said. "You've got the wrong judge for that."

articles.title: How Good Can the Eagles Defense Become Under Vic Fangio? Nolan Smith Has an Answer
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles may have plenty of reasons to believe their defense can dominate again, however, Nolan Smith is not putting a ceiling on it, and with...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles may have plenty of reasons to believe their defense can dominate again, however, Nolan Smith is not putting a ceiling on it, and with Jonathan Greenard's availability for Week 1 suddenly in doubt, Smith could have a much bigger role in making that confidence real.

Smith enters 2026 healthy after spending much of last season battling a triceps injury. Now, with Vic Fangio running the show and Greenard sidelined, the former first-round pick has a chance to turn that confidence into production.

Nolan Smith And The Philadelphia Eagles Are Betting On Fangio's Defense

Smith is not shy about what he thinks the Eagles' defense can become. He believes the group has been building toward something special, with Fangio providing the structure and trust needed to make it work.

"I'm excited to start the season. We don't have any ceiling. We have been building brick by brick how we want it. With Coach Fangio at the helm, I feel like anything is possible for us. Everybody in our room trusts him, believes him, and he is a phenomenal coach. We will just fly around and let our hair out"

That belief is not coming out of nowhere. The Eagles have allowed the fewest points per game over the past two seasons when their starters have been on the field under Fangio. That gives Smith plenty of reason to trust the system.

However, the defense could face an early test. Greenard, whom Philadelphia acquired and signed to a four-year extension worth nearly $100 million, has been sidelined with a pec injury. Fangio has already admitted he's concerned about Greenard being ready for the opener.

For Smith, that is also an opportunity. The 2023 first-round pick is finally healthy after tearing his triceps during Super Bowl LIX and aggravating the injury last season. He played only 12 games in 2025 and finished with three sacks after producing 10.5 over the regular 45-season games of the previous season.

Now, he believes his body is ready for the grind. Smith said his biggest priority this offseason was making sure his arm was strong enough to handle all 18 weeks. That is important because the Eagles could need him immediately if Greenard isn't ready.

And Smith is not planning to change how he plays. Standing at only 6-foot-2 and weighing 238 pounds, he is undersized compared to many other edge rushers in the NFL, but his physicality has never been able to keep up with his measurements. He will go at defenders, set the edge, and play aggressively enough for Fangio to get the most out of.

There is another problem that looms over his career, too. Philadelphia made its fifth-year option for 2027, and although they have not extended him yet, as they have done with Jalen Carter .

If Smith has a great 2026 season, that would likely all be sorted very soon. For now, though, he is focused on the project in Philadelphia. Fangio has earned his trust, and the defense has a proven history as well.

articles.title: Chicago Bears: Former 4th-Round Pick Could be Moved
articles.summary: Chicago Bears running back Roschon Johnson had a forgettable 2025 campaign, battling three separate injuries and playing the fewest snaps of his young NFL ca...
articles.body:
Chicago Bears running back Roschon Johnson had a forgettable 2025 campaign, battling three separate injuries and playing the fewest snaps of his young NFL career. Johnson missed Week 1 with a foot injury, Weeks 8 and 9 with a back injury, and suffered a season-ending thumb injury in Week 11. He finished with 17 rushing yards on two carries across seven games and four offensive snaps.

Roschon Johnson faces an uphill battle to make the 53-man roster as the team's No. 3 running back. He is competing against Salvon Ahmed , who has had a strong training camp. Ahmed has totaled 53 rushing yards and 69 receiving yards in the preseason, including a 49-yard touchdown reception against the Browns. Meanwhile, Johnson has totaled 76 rushing and four receiving yards.

The Chicago Bears ' former 4th-round pick could be moved

In an NFL.com article, Kevin Patra identified 22 players who could be traded or released during roster cuts. For the Bears, he named Roschon Johnson , noting his limited offensive role last season and struggles to stand out this offseason. Patra also added that Johnson lacks dual-threat ability, which makes him a poor fit, especially with D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai receiving most of the touches.

"The former fourth-rounder has struggled to gain traction this offseason. Lacking keen dual-threat ability doesn't make him a great third-back option for Ben Johnson's offense behind D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai . Johnson took just two carries in seven games last year," Patra said.

Here's what a trading team would inherit contractually

A trading team would inherit a one-year, $1.145 million contract, per Over The Cap . If Johnson gets traded, plays well this season, and signs elsewhere next March, the trading team may secure a compensatory pick for the 2028 NFL Draft. The Bears would prefer to trade the former fourth-round pick and receive draft compensation rather than cutting him outright.

The Los Angeles Dodgers set their lineup against the Atlanta Braves as they look to level up the series on Wednesday.

The Dodgers lost, 4-3, on Tuesday, failing to put together a late comeback after a leadoff Shohei Ohtani triple in the top of the ninth inning. Tyler Glasnow made his first start since returning from injury in the game and had a decent showing after a shaky first inning, but the Dodgers couldn't give him the run support he needed.

Roki Sasaki takes the mound for the Dodgers on Wednesday, looking to extend his streak of strong starts in the second half of the season.

Sasaki has a 4.42 ERA on the year, striking out 114 batters in 116 innings, but has looked infinitely better than he did in the first half. Since the All-Star break, Sasaki has a 2.31 ERA with 34 strikeouts in 35 innings, and has only allowed two home runs compared to 19 in the first half.

The Dodgers' lineup stayed fairly similar to Tuesday's loss, with Ohtani, first baseman Freddie Freeman and shortstop Mookie Betts occupy the spots at the top of the order. Third baseman Max Muncy still sits in the cleanup spot, and Tommy Edman remains at second base while following him.

Kyle Tucker plays in right field and bats seventh, and Alek Thomas moves up to the No. 7 spot in center field. Left fielder Teoscar Hernandez moves down to the No. 8 spot for Wednesday's game, and Hunter Feduccia rounds out the lineup behind the plate.

The Braves have right-hander AJ Smith-Shawver on the mound for Wednesday's game, giving the Dodgers a good opportunity to even the series. Smith-Shawver has a 6.23 ERA on the season through two starts, allowing six earned runs through 8.2 innings pitched and striking out seven batters.

articles.title: Journalist: Liverpool eyeing late move for €50m-rated midfielder
articles.summary: Liverpool Transfer News: Lamine Camara Emerges as Deadline Day Midfield TargetLiverpool’s final days of the transfer window appear increasingly likely to inv...
articles.body:
Liverpool Transfer News: Lamine Camara Emerges as Deadline Day Midfield Target

Liverpool's final days of the transfer window appear increasingly likely to involve a familiar question. Does Andoni Iraola have enough in midfield?

According to journalist Abdel Hamed , Liverpool remain interested in strengthening at No. 6 and would like to make a late move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara. It is an intriguing possibility, particularly after Curtis Jones completed his £30 million move to Inter Milan.

Jones made 228 appearances for Liverpool, scoring 22 goals, and his departure has removed another experienced option from Iraola's squad.

Liverpool have spent much of the summer prioritising attacking reinforcements. Iraola has also indicated that 19-year-old Trey Nyoni could assume greater responsibility following Jones' departure.

Yet the composition of Liverpool's midfield deserves scrutiny.

Dominik Szoboszlai , Alexis Mac Allister and Ryan Gravenberch provide considerable technical quality, but Liverpool still appear short of a midfielder whose natural instincts revolve around controlling space, protecting transitions and providing stability behind more adventurous players.

That concern became particularly apparent during the 2-2 draw at Newcastle United , when Liverpool were repeatedly vulnerable through central areas.

Camara, therefore, makes sense stylistically as well as numerically.

Monaco Valuation Could Shape Deadline Day

Hamed reports that Liverpool would like to move for Camara late in the window, with interested clubs apparently waiting because they are conscious of Monaco's circumstances.

That creates the possibility of a deadline day negotiation.

The 22-year-old Senegal international has already accumulated 30 caps and scored four international goals. His Monaco contract runs until 2029, giving the Ligue 1 club considerable negotiating strength.

Monaco reportedly value Camara at approximately €50 million and regard him as one of their prized assets alongside Folarin Balogun .

There is consequently little incentive for Monaco to accept a substantially reduced fee unless circumstances change.

Alex Scott Remains Another Liverpool Option

Camara's emergence also adds another dimension to Liverpool's long-standing interest in Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott.

Scott knows Iraola particularly well from their time together at Bournemouth and has rejected a new contract at the Vitality Stadium. Bournemouth's reported £90 million valuation, however, makes that particular reunion extremely expensive.

Chelsea have reportedly already seen an offer of around £70 million rejected, while Arsenal , Manchester United and Manchester City have also shown interest.

Camara at €50 million would represent a considerably different financial proposition.

Liverpool's decision may ultimately reveal how seriously the club views its midfield vulnerability. Trusting Nyoni with increased minutes is perfectly reasonable. Asking a 19-year-old to compensate for an underlying structural problem would be a much greater gamble.

Camara could provide Iraola with the specialist presence Liverpool currently appear to lack.

From a Liverpool supporter's perspective, this is one of the more intriguing midfield links of the summer.

There has been plenty of discussion about replacing Jones in terms of minutes, but Liverpool should probably be thinking about something more fundamental. The question is whether this midfield actually has the right balance for Iraola's football.

Nyoni deserves opportunities. His development should be encouraged rather than blocked by another expensive signing simply because Jones has left. Camara, though, would potentially occupy a different role.

Liverpool have enough players who want to influence possession higher up the pitch. What they appear to need is someone capable of providing security when those players move forward.

The Newcastle game supplied an early warning. Liverpool were too easy to play through centrally, and that becomes particularly concerning when Iraola wants his side to press aggressively and commit numbers forward.

€50 million also feels far more digestible than the reported £90 million required for Scott. Scott's familiarity with Iraola carries obvious value, but Bournemouth's valuation creates an enormous burden of expectation.

Camara would be fascinating because this feels like a move based upon squad architecture rather than replacing one departing player with another.

If Liverpool genuinely believe he can become the controlling No. 6 this midfield requires, deadline day could suddenly become very interesting.
